class.name: NetwTxnBook
class.brief_description: The requests a peer is still waiting on an answer to: who each one addressed, and the tick its patience runs out on.
class.description: This book holds no promise and settles nothing. What it decides is who may answer a request and when one has waited long enough, and those two questions have to agree across three paths that never see each other: a reply arriving, a timeout sweep, and a peer dropping. The caller above turns each answer into a settle. [codeblock] var txn := book.mint() book.open(txn, PackedInt64Array([peer_id]), current_tick + timeout) # a reply arrives if book.admits(txn, sender): settle(txn, value) book.close(txn) # every tick for id in book.expire(current_tick): fail(id, ERR_TIMEOUT) # a peer drops for id in book.waiting_on(peer_id): ... [/codeblock] Ids are minted here and never reused, so a reply that arrives after its transaction closed names a transaction that no longer exists rather than a live one that happens to share its number. Every answer is in minting order, so a sweep that settles a hundred requests settles them the same way twice. Every answer this book gives comes back in minting order, ascending, so a sweep that settles a hundred requests settles them the same way twice.

method.name: addressed
method.description: The peers [param txn_id] was sent to. A transaction that is not open addressed nobody.

method.name: admits
method.description: Whether [param txn_id] addressed [param sender]. An answer from anyone else, or to a transaction that has closed, is not this request's, and honouring it would let any peer settle a request made of another.

method.name: close
method.description: Forgets [param txn_id], answering whether it was open. Its id is not reused.

method.name: drain
method.description: Every open transaction, emptying the book as it names them, so a settle that opens a new request cannot see the ones being abandoned. This is what a session teardown asks for.

method.name: expire
method.description: Every open transaction whose deadline is at or before [param current], closed as it is named. Naming and closing are one act, so a second sweep at the same tick names none of them again and a caller cannot fail a request twice.

method.name: is_open
method.description: Whether [param txn_id] is still waiting on an answer.

method.name: mint
method.description: The next transaction id, counting from one and never repeating within a session. Minting does not open anything, because a caller that fails to build its request should not leave a transaction behind.

method.name: open
method.description: Records that [param txn_id] was sent to [param addressed] and gives up at [param deadline], a tick on the same clock [method expire] is swept with.

method.name: waiting_on
method.description: Every open transaction that addressed [param peer_id]. A peer dropping is not a timeout, so this names what the caller must settle now rather than closing anything itself.
